title: Wholeness Reflection
opening: One disappointment can become the whole account. Look across the day without making it all good.

labels.example: A week with one missed milestone
labels.exampleContext: At week's end, a person sees that the project milestone was missed and calls the week wasted.
labels.taskLensBody: That result is real and may need a change to the plan. This narrow review tells you about the project milestone; it cannot describe everything that mattered in the week.
labels.wholeLensHeading: Keep the missed milestone in view, then add other actual moments.

episodes.title: A small project step was finished
episodes.contribution: The step advanced the work. It counts as a success even though the larger milestone remained unfinished.
episodes.resistance: It does not make the milestone complete or settle whether the project plan needs to change.

episodes.title: A quiet afternoon with a friend
episodes.contribution: No project task was completed. The time still mattered as lived connection.
episodes.resistance: The person felt guilty about time away from the project. That feeling can be noticed without treating the afternoon as wasted.

episodes.title: A work session that stalled
episodes.contribution: The attempt may have revealed that the instructions skipped a prerequisite. If that detail is verified, the next plan can include it.
episodes.resistance: The session was frustrating and produced no deliverable. A possible correction does not make the frustration good or the milestone complete.

episodes.title: Time alone to rest
episodes.contribution: Rest did not need a project output to count as lived time.
episodes.resistance: If the person wanted more connection, that matters too. The reflection does not have to make this moment fit everyone.

labels.choiceBody: Keep the missed milestone visible. If the missing prerequisite is confirmed, add it to the next work plan. Keep the friend time that mattered instead of treating it as time to repay. This does not settle every deadline or make every week successful.
labels.counterexampleHeading: A wider view does not cancel a needed change
labels.counterexampleBody: A narrow review is right for a narrow task. If a deadline or harmful condition needs action, a broad reflection must not hide it. Some days contain no useful lesson from a setback; leave that unresolved rather than inventing one.
labels.attemptIntro: Choose a day you can discuss comfortably. Name one moment that mattered outside a task list, one other experience you want beside it, and what each contributed or what you resisted. Keep disappointment, cost or uncertainty where it remains. Then say what, if anything, changes about a current choice.

labels.private: Your reflection is private and ungraded.
labels.oversize: Shorten the complete reflection to 2,000 characters or fewer. Your full draft stays on screen.
labels.sourceExcerpt: “Review moments of comfort and challenge, success and setback, solitude and connection. Examine what each contributed, which you resisted and what you notice when both are considered.”

source.assessmentBoundary: The six source questions are required open-ended assessment prompts with no stored gold answer. This optional private reflection is not a grade or a replacement assessment.
source.attribution: Supplied manuscript; authorship/adoption of every wording is not independently established.
source.exampleBoundary: The missed-milestone week is an authored illustration, not observed data. The possible prerequisite and contributions are hypotheses in that scenario; they are not outcomes attributed to a learner.

twentyFirstDev.query: daily journal reflection cards for experiences and meaning no ratings
twentyFirstDev.use: Metadata described a minimal, text-focused journal-entry preview. It informed keeping experience text readable as cards; no code or copy was used.

mobbin.query: mobile daily reflection showing both experience and resistance
mobbin.reason: No Mobbin screen-search tool was exposed in this session.

assessment.guidedQuestion: Does full range require seeking every difficult experience?
assessment.learnerCheck: Can you distinguish meaning, fulfillment and achievement without collapsing them?
assessment.outcomeCheck: Does the reflection help preserve worthwhile participation and appropriate choices?
assessment.changeAccount: If it rationalizes harm or hides a necessary change, revise the interpretation.
